units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
To Footman .
Just wait, Francis.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Writes letter .
That is a very wonderful opening for so young a man as you are, Mr. Arbuthnot.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: It is indeed, Lady Caroline. I trust I shall be able to show myself worthy of it.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: I trust so.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: To HESTER.
You have not congratulated me yet, Miss Worsley.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Are you very pleased about it?
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Of course I am. It means everything to me—things that were out of the reach of hope before may be within hope’s reach now.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Nothing should be out of the reach of hope. Life is a hope.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: I fancy, Caroline, that Diplomacy is what Lord Illingworth is aiming at. I heard that he was offered Vienna. But that may not be true.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: I don’t think that England should be represented abroad by an unmarried man, Jane. It might lead to complications.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: You are too nervous, Caroline. Believe me, you are too nervous. Besides, Lord Illingworth may marry any day. I was in hopes he would have married Lady Kelso. But I believe he said her family was too large. Or was it her feet? I forget which. I regret it very much. She was made to be an ambassador’s wife.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: She certainly has a wonderful faculty of remembering people’s names, and forgetting their faces.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: Well, that is very natural, Caroline, is it not?
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: To Footman .
Tell Henry to wait for an answer. I have written a line to your dear mother, Gerald, to tell her your good news, and to say she really must come to dinner.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Exit Footman .
That is awfully kind of you, Lady Hunstanton.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: To HESTER.
Will you come for a stroll, Miss Worsley?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: With pleasure.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Exit with GERALD.

I am very much gratified at Gerald Arbuthnot’s good fortune. He is quite a protégé of mine. And I am particularly pleased that Lord Illingworth should have made the offer of his own accord without my suggesting anything. Nobody likes to be asked favours. I remember poor Charlotte Pagden making herself quite unpopular one season, because she had a French governess she wanted to recommend to every one.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: I saw the governess, Jane. Lady Pagden sent her to me. It was before Eleanor came out. She was far too good-looking to be in any respectable household. I don’t wonder Lady Pagden was so anxious to get rid of her.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: Ah, that explains it.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: John, the grass is too damp for you. You had better go and put on your overshoes at once.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: I am quite comfortable, Caroline, I assure you.
units.name: SIR JOHN

units.text: You must allow me to be the best judge of that, John. Pray do as I tell you.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: SIR JOHN gets up and goes off .
You spoil him, Caroline, you do indeed!
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Enter MRS. ALLONBY and LADY STUTFIELD.
[ To MRS. ALLONBY.] Well, dear, I hope you like the park.
It is said to be well timbered.
The trees are wonderful, Lady Hunstanton.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Quite, quite wonderful.
units.name: LADY STUTFIELD

units.text: But somehow, I feel sure that if I lived in the country for six months, I should become so unsophisticated that no one would take the slightest notice of me.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I assure you, dear, that the country has not that effect at all. Why, it was from Melthorpe, which is only two miles from here, that Lady Belton eloped with Lord Fethersdale. I remember the occurrence perfectly. Poor Lord Belton died three days afterwards of joy, or gout. I forget which. We had a large party staying here at the time, so we were all very much interested in the whole affair.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: I think to elope is cowardly. It’s running away from danger. And danger has become so rare in modern life.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: As far as I can make out, the young women of the present day seem to make it the sole object of their lives to be always playing with fire.
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: The one advantage of playing with fire, Lady Caroline, is that one never gets even singed. It is the people who don’t know how to play with it who get burned up.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Yes; I see that. It is very, very helpful.
units.name: LADY STUTFIELD

units.text: I don’t know how the world would get on with such a theory as that, dear Mrs. Allonby.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Ah! The world was made for men and not for women.
units.name: LADY STUTFIELD

units.text: Oh, don’t say that, Lady Stutfield. We have a much better time than they have. There are far more things forbidden to us than are forbidden to them.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY
